question: GQ-007
subject: my own refactor broke resume, and would have cost archive.org 36 downloads

the_bug.introduced: last turn, converting ia-ingest.mjs to lib/vault-paths.mjs
the_bug.what: set VAULT = vaultRoot() — the librarian-vault ROOT — while all six joins below still assumed the ia-ingest directory
the_bug.symptom: "0 already on vault; 36 to fetch" for 36 books sitting on disk
the_bug.cost_if_unnoticed: 36 redundant downloads from a volunteer-run archive, plus manifests written to the wrong directory
the_bug.why_the_fixture_test_missed_it: the fixture supplies its own VAULT_ROOT and the builder wrote and read consistently within it — the bug only shows against the REAL layout

fix: VAULT = ingestDir(), the helper built for exactly this
the_other_two_converted_scripts_were_cor: build-external-passages and migrate-book-external explicitly join ia-ingest/ and books-catalogue/ under the root, so vaultRoot() is right for them

regression_test_added.case: ingest resume sees books already on the vault
regression_test_added.proven: reintroduced the bug on a copy — FAIL with the offending output quoted

the_lesson: a refactor that passes every test can still break production when the tests supply their own environment. The fixture proved the builder is self-consistent; only the real layout proved it is CORRECT.

fifth_want_list.batch: 120 — a bounded first batch rather than 443 at once
